_metadata.scope: General adsorbate construction and verification; no material-specific answer rules.

formula_and_molecule_inventory.summary: Parse resolved formulas with Composition and sum molecule count times formula for every adsorbate; retain group identities.
principles: Resolve molecular names to explicit formulas and connectivity. Composition parses formulas; it does not infer connectivity, isomers or binding geometry. Avoid a finite lookup table of supported formula strings.
Sum count times formula for every requested molecule, including repeated species. Track adsorbate groups separately from substrate atoms, especially when their elements overlap.

coverage_and_surface_side.summary: Define coverage denominator and populated surface side explicitly; require integer counts without silent rounding.
principles: State the coverage denominator, such as exposed substrate sites on a specified side, and whether one or both slab surfaces are populated. Compute each molecule count from that convention.
If the requested coverage is incompatible with integer counts, enlarge the allowed surface supercell or report the incompatibility; never silently round. Preserve coverage when changing the cell.

groupwise_binding_geometry.summary: Place complete molecules by anchors and rigid orientation; check every adsorbate and honor explicit task constraints.
principles: Assign each adsorbate a group, binding atom or binding-atom set, target site and surface side. Use rigid translation and rotation of a coherent molecular geometry; molecular composition alone is insufficient.

Evaluate every group's anchor height, orientation, connectivity and periodic separation from other groups. Explicit task constraints take priority over typical literature heights or default site preferences.

post_relaxation_verification.summary: Recheck geometry, inventory, sites and molecular integrity after relaxation; low forces do not prove correct adsorption.
principles: After any relaxation, wrapping or cell change, verify finite coordinates and lattice, molecular connectivity, atom inventory, coverage, selected sites and local-normal binding geometry using periodic images.

Lower forces alone do not establish correct adsorption. Do not resolve repulsion by moving molecules arbitrarily far away or silently changing the requested binding mode; retain and recheck the construction constraints.
